headline: Weekend Brief: US stock futures dipped as oil climbed on reported US strikes in Strait of Hormuz ahead of key manufacturing data and the August jobs report
raw_text:
- Reports of US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz pushed WTI crude (@CL) about 2% higher near $85, pressuring US equity futures Sunday night
- Wall Street closed out a strong August with the S&P 500 (SPX) up roughly 3% and the Nasdaq (COMP) up about 4%, led by tech gains including Nvidia (NVDA) up about 8% and Microsoft (MSFT) up roughly 11% amid an “epic” software rally
- Hawkish comments from former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole increased perceived rate-hike odds and weighed on sentiment, leaving bond investors cautious
- President Trump’s latest US–Canada trade war rhetoric, including an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to “Lake America” for US users, added to trade-policy uncertainty
- Aon (AON) is reportedly nearing a roughly $17 billion acquisition of insurance brokerage USI from KKR (KKR), with a possible Monday announcement that could impact AON shares and the broader insurance and financials space
- The previously announced roughly $4–4.6 billion Vanguard–Altruist transaction continued to generate buzz as a competitive challenge to Charles Schwab (SCHW) and Fidelity in the RIA custody market and a potential tailwind for ETF distribution
- Monday’s US macro calendar features ISM Manufacturing PMI, JOLTs job openings, S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 10:30 a.m. ET, and Treasury bill auctions, setting the tone ahead of the August jobs report and further tech earnings
- Investors are monitoring Apple (AAPL)’s “big handoff” developments as a potential additional catalyst for large-cap tech during the week
